    3 x bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8      (frontier)
    2 x bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6    (standard)

f81d's failure mode:
    cache_read_tokens   18,292      <- nonzero, so caching is genuinely ENGAGING on the Bedrock path
    cache_write_tokens  10,571
    input_tokens       240,483

So on the Bedrock path a real code-review gate parses its verdict, resolves both the frontier and
standard classes to inference profiles, makes zero direct-Anthropic calls, and reads from cache rather

METHOD NOTE, since this is the fourth attempt at this gate: it was run as a detached background job
rather than inside an agent. Four consecutive agent attempts were killed by the 600s stream watchdog —

a process death instead of being re-bought.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
AC6 cachePoint TTL — STATED WITH EVIDENCE, and it CORRECTS THIS TICKETS OWN PREMISE.

The description asserts "Bedrocks cachePoint carries NO TTL where Anthropics cache_control
carries ttl:5m" and calls that difference substantive. That premise is WRONG, and the correction is
the answer to the criterion:

  Bedrocks cachePoint block takes an OPTIONAL `ttl` that DEFAULTS TO 5 MINUTES — the same default
  Anthropics cache_control applies. The TTL is not missing on Bedrock; it is defaulted, and
  defaulted to the SAME value. rebar emits no explicit TTL on either path, so both yield a 5-minute
  lifetime. There is no observable difference to account for, and no per-provider cache tuning is
  needed.
  Bedrock additionally offers a 1-hour TTL for some Claude models. It is opt-in and rebar does not
  request it, so it is not a difference either.
  Sources: AWS "Amazon Bedrock now supports 1-hour duration for prompt caching" (Jan 2026) and the
  Bedrock cachePoint API reference (ttl optional, valid "5m"/"1h", default 5m).

EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE, from my own three Bedrock gate runs (cache READS, not writes — a write-only
tally is bug f81ds failure mode and proves nothing):
  review-plan       cache_read 226,668 across 18 of 27 calls
  review-code       cache_read  18,292
  verify-completion cache_read  45,122
Caching demonstrably ENGAGES on the Bedrock path on all three gates.

HONEST LIMIT, stated rather than papered over: no gate run exercises a gap LONGER than 5 minutes
between calls, because each gate completes well inside one TTL window. So the runs confirm the
lifetime is not shorter than a gate run; they do not probe expiry. That does not affect the
criterion, which asks whether the TTL difference causes an observable difference — there is no
difference in the defaults to cause one.

RECORDED IN THE DELIVERABLE: docs/local-dev-env.md, new bullet in the Bedrock sections "Things
that bite" list, carrying the default-parity statement and the three measured cache_read figures.

AC7 REVERT — EXECUTED AND PROVEN, token-free in BOTH directions via load_class_slots/resolve_class:
  export REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE=~/.config/rebar/bedrock.toml ->
    {trivial: bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0,
     standard: bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6,
     frontier: bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8}
  unset REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE ->
    {trivial: anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5,
     standard: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6,
     frontier: anthropic:claude-opus-4-8}
One variable, all three classes flip back to Anthropic. A developer gets back in one step.

AC8 infra/ UNTOUCHED — verified by diff, not by assertion:
  git diff --name-only origin/main..HEAD -- infra/  =>  0 files.

compiled_state.description:
# S7b — Run the LOCAL developer gates on Bedrock (dogfood before the production cutover)

## Context / Problem

S8 (eb6e) cuts the PRODUCTION review bot over to Bedrock with NO fallback — it is the gate that votes
on every landing on `main`. Today the first time rebar exercises Bedrock through a real gate will be
that cutover, on the shared bot, where a failure stops everyone's landings until a human runs the kill
switch.

Local developer gates (`rebar review-plan`, `rebar review-code`, `rebar verify-completion`) run the
SAME LLM stack against the SAME provider seam, on a machine where a failure costs one person one
command. Pointing them at Bedrock first converts the production cutover from a first contact into a
confirmation.

## What is already established — do NOT re-measure

* BEDROCK IS INVOKABLE from this host: account 896586841071, us-east-1, caller
  `arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier`. AWS CLI credentials are present and working.
* ONLY INFERENCE PROFILES WORK. Plain on-demand ids (`anthropic.claude-*`) are NOT invokable in this
  account at all — they return a ValidationException directing you to use an inference profile
  [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550].
* PROMPT CACHING WORKS on a regional inference profile: `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` measured
  cache_write=4017 then cached on the next attempt; a longer end-to-end run recorded
  cache_read=542,723 / cache_write=6,239 over 19 calls. Caching and inference profiles are NOT
  mutually exclusive, and `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` is the recorded verified caching default.
* `temperature=0` is REFUSED on opus (`ValidationException: temperature is deprecated for this
  model`) and is already handled by the `supports_temperature: False` capability override — the
  withdrawal is MODEL-driven, not provider-driven, and happens identically on both providers.
* PAYLOAD AND TOOL PARITY ARE PROVEN [rebar:0d76-ebbf-ee3a-48ac]: for the same logical call the system
  prompt, messages and tool definitions are byte-identical across providers; the model id is the only
  differing field. Eight envelope differences are enumerated there, seven of them spelling.
* ONE ENVELOPE DIFFERENCE IS SUBSTANTIVE and is the thing most likely to bite here: Bedrock's
  `cachePoint` carries NO TTL where Anthropic's `cache_control` carries `ttl:"5m"`. Latent today
  because rebar sets no non-default TTL — but this story is the cheapest place to find out if that
  assumption is wrong.

## Approach

Configure the LOCAL rebar install to resolve its model classes to Bedrock inference profiles, using the
AWS CLI credentials already on the host, and then RUN THE REAL GATES and compare against the Anthropic
baseline. Prefer the layered config file (`REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` / the `model_classes` table) over the
deprecated bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`, so the change is per-class and reversible rather than global.

The deliverable is not the config line — it is the EVIDENCE that a developer's day-to-day gates behave
on Bedrock: verdicts still parse, structured output still validates, caching still engages, and the
observable cost does not regress.

**Explicitly out of scope:** the production bot, its IAM, its alarms, and its kill switch. Those are
S8's. This story must not touch `infra/`.

## Scope

- local LLM configuration only (the config file and/or documented env for a developer machine)
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` — how a developer opts in, and how to revert
- no `src/` behaviour change is expected; if one turns out to be required, that is a finding worth a
  separate ticket rather than silent scope growth

## Testing

Live, because a configuration that only works in a unit test proves nothing here. The oracle is a real
local gate run against a real ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [operator-attested] `rebar review-plan` runs end-to-end against Bedrock on a real ticket and
      returns a parseable verdict, recorded with the ticket id, the resolved model ids per pass, and
      the run timestamp.
- [x] [operator-attested] the run's `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` per-call tally shows EVERY call resolved to a
      Bedrock inference profile and ZERO calls to direct Anthropic — the same provider-clean check S6
      applied to its measured arms.
- [x] [operator-attested] prompt caching is observed ENGAGING on the Bedrock path: a run records
      nonzero `cache_read_tokens`, cited from the usage log. A write alone is insufficient — write-only
      is the failure mode bug f81d exists for.
- [x] [operator-attested] `rebar review-code` and `rebar verify-completion` are each exercised once on
      Bedrock and their outcomes recorded. These are the other two gates a developer hits daily; a
      plan-review-only proof would leave them untested.
- [x] Structured output validates on every gate run — no verdict falls back to an unparsed or
      INDETERMINATE shape for a provider-shaped reason. Any that does is recorded with its raw payload.
- [x] Whether the missing Bedrock `cachePoint` TTL causes any observable difference is STATED, with
      evidence either way. "Not observed" is an acceptable answer; silence is not.
- [x] The opt-in and the REVERT are both documented in `docs/local-dev-env.md`, and the revert is
      executed once to prove a developer can get back to Anthropic in one step.
- [x] Nothing under `infra/` is modified — verified by the diff.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
compiled_state.title: S7b — Run the LOCAL developer gates on Bedrock (dogfood before the production cutover)
